email.body1:
Thom, saw Wiiisdom expanded its AnalyticsOps portfolio with Ops for Power BI, on top of the Tableau and SAP BusinessObjects lines.

A broader platform usually opens more BI and data-governance accounts than your team can work before they go quiet. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up on its own, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a signal play for Wiiisdom off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Thom, quick follow-up for Wiiisdom.

As Power BI opens a new buyer segment, most teams do not actually know how many meetings they need to convert it, so the coverage gap shows up late and the quarter turns into a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Wiiisdom needs to hit target, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Thom, last bit of proof for Wiiisdom.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email logged to CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how your reply rate likely compares to other data and analytics startups. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Thom, I will stop reaching out on this one, but did not want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount is not a priority while you push the Power BI launch, no problem at all. A product expansion is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a data and analytics motion? I will tailor it to Wiiisdom either way.
